newsitem.title: GREECE: ATHLETICS-BUBKA WINS WORLD TITLE FOR THE SIXTH TIME.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-BUBKA WINS WORLD TITLE FOR THE SIXTH TIME.

text.p: Sergei Bubka, the greatest pole vaulter in the history of the sport, won the world title for the sixth time in succession on Sunday against all the odds.
Bubka did not start last year's Atlanta Olympic competition after sustaining an Achilles tendon injury while warming up for the qualifying round.
The injury has continued to haunt him this year and he was not considered one of the title favourites here.
But once against the extraordinary competitive spirit which has seen the Ukrainian win the world title at each championships since the inaugural 1983 Helinski competition prevailed.
He cleared 5.70 with his second attempt, 5.91, again with his second attempt, then 6.01 with his first effort to clinch the gold medal.
He then had the bar set at 6.15 but ran through his only attempt on his own world record.
Russian Maxim Tarasov took the silver and American Dean Starkey the bronze.
